dropped.evox-frontier-cs: Benchmark-level aggregate, not one task: EvoX and AdaEvolve (skydiscover benchmarks/frontier-cs-eval) run a separate search per Frontier-CS problem (FRONTIER_CS_PROBLEM) and report the mean official score over the 172 problems of their run; one candidate program cannot be scored across problems with different inputs and outputs. Scoring the aggregate needs the Frontier-CS judge for every problem (188 algorithmic problem directories at commit e6ef46eb, 74 interactive with interactors), i.e. the Docker judge service. Per-problem tasks can be recreated like coral-frontier-cs-polyominoes-packing.
dropped.magellan-llvm-function-inlining-for-clan: The reward is end-to-end runtime of clang itself built with the evolved inliner, PGO and distributed ThinLTO at -O3; each candidate needs a full clang rebuild (CPU-hours) plus macro-benchmark timing, and the reported effects (-2.4% to +0.61%) are within the run-to-run timing noise of a CPU evaluator.
dropped.magellan-llvm-register-allocation: The reward is runtime on Google's production search workload; Magellan's change is from -0.55% to -0.15%, below the 1-2% run-to-run CPU-time noise measured here. LLVM 23 exposes an interactive priority-advisor channel, but it provides no reward, and a static spill-cost proxy would measure a different objective.
